A.reason: All candidates preserve destination privacy, allow emergency use and compare the three required measures over two weeks. Their primary mechanisms are first-entry reservations, rotating priority, usage-based priority, flexible scheduling and bounded-loan queuing. Candidate 3 best combines early conflict resolution with a way to accommodate competing trips, explicit fallback rules and an inspectable trial, though evening discussion adds effort.

B.reason: All candidates are usable. Candidates 5 and 6 repair reservations and rotating priority respectively, rather than introduce new mechanisms. The other mechanisms are usage-based priority, flexible scheduling, bounded-loan queuing and voluntary reduction of bike absence through early return. Candidate 3 provides a concrete scheduling procedure, confirmed allocations, explicit handling of unallocated requests and a trial that checks both saved trips and displacement of long trips.

pair.reason: B3 narrowly improves on A3 through a more explicit allocation procedure and comparison against simple reservations, with direct checks for saved trips, added effort and harm to long trips. Its added scheduling burden is a limitation, but the proposal makes that tradeoff inspectable.
